title: Cartesian neighborhood squares of the proper refinement graph
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a scheme morphism, $s,r$ compactifications, and $\rho:r\to s$ a refinement. Construct $T=r.Z\times_Y s.Z$, $z=(1,\rho):r.Z\to T$, the neighborhoods $O_1=T\times_{s.Z}X$, $O_2=T\times_{r.Z}X$, and the literal lifts $s_1,s_2$ as in [def-pur-etale-refinement-graph-transport]. Then $z,s_1,s_2$ are proper, their common map to $T$ is $r.i;z$, and $zp=r.g$. The square $(s_2,r.i,b_2,z)$ is Cartesian. If the supplied refinement square $(r.i,1_X,\rho,s.i)$ is Cartesian, so is $(s_1,r.i,b_1,z)$. The equality $((1_X;r.i);r.g)=s.i;s.g$ used in these lifts follows from the compactification equations.

proof.text: The composites of z, s1 and s2 with the appropriate product or neighborhood projection are identities. These projections are proper, hence separated, so proper-to-separated cancellation proves that the three sections are proper. Compare the two projections to T to show graph_fac, using rho.i_hom; the first projection also gives zp=r.g. For square1 paste with the canonical neighborhood pullback: the outer square is exactly the supplied Cartesian refinement square, since z pr2=rho and s1 q1=1. Cancel the lower canonical pullback and flip. For square2 the same outer square is the identity square on r.i, since z pr1=1 and s2 q2=1; apply the same cancellation. The displayed equation follows from r.comm and s.comm. These arguments apply to identity refinements and empty opens unchanged.
